title: Hall of Legends 👑⚡
difficulty: Ascended (Prestige VI – Hall of Legends Challenge)

questions.question: Which animal has the most powerful bite force ever measured among living animals?
questions.hint: The Saltwater Crocodile has the strongest measured bite force of any living animal, exceeding 16,000 newtons.

questions.question: Which tree species produces the world's largest seed?
questions.hint: The Coco de Mer palm of the Seychelles produces the largest and heaviest seed of any plant, weighing up to 25 kg (55 lb).

questions.question: Which film was the first to surpass $1 billion at the worldwide box office?
questions.hint: Released in 1997, Titanic became the first movie to gross over $1 billion worldwide.

questions.question: Which television series features the fictional paper company Dunder Mifflin?
questions.hint: Dunder Mifflin Paper Company is the workplace at the heart of The Office.

questions.question: Which international organization publishes the annual World Economic Outlook?
questions.hint: The IMF releases the World Economic Outlook, analyzing global economic trends and forecasts.

questions.question: Which organization coordinates international policing and criminal cooperation?
questions.hint: INTERPOL facilitates cooperation among police agencies in nearly every country.

questions.question: Which empire built the famous Hagia Sophia?
questions.hint: The Hagia Sophia was completed in AD 537 under Emperor Justinian I of the Byzantine Empire.

questions.question: Which explorer first successfully reached the South Pole?
questions.hint: Norwegian explorer Roald Amundsen reached the South Pole on December 14, 1911.

questions.question: Which country won the first FIFA World Cup in 1930?
questions.hint: Uruguay defeated Argentina 4–2 in the inaugural FIFA World Cup Final.

questions.question: Which chess piece can move the greatest number of squares in a single move?
questions.hint: The queen combines the movement of both the rook and bishop, making it the most powerful piece.

questions.question: Which country is home to the world's highest navigable lake, Lake Titicaca?
questions.hint: Lake Titicaca lies on the border between Peru and Bolivia at an elevation of about 3,812 meters (12,507 feet).

questions.question: Which country has the most islands in the world?
questions.hint: Sweden has approximately 267,000 islands, more than any other country.

questions.question: Which planet has the hottest average surface temperature in the Solar System?
questions.hint: Although Mercury is closer to the Sun, Venus is hotter due to its dense carbon dioxide atmosphere causing an extreme greenhouse effect.

questions.question: Which scientist introduced the concept of natural selection?
questions.hint: Darwin's theory of evolution by natural selection transformed modern biology.

questions.question: Which civilization built the massive stone monuments at Stonehenge?
questions.hint: Stonehenge was built in stages over many centuries by prehistoric communities, but its exact builders remain unknown.

questions.question: Which country is famous for originating flamenco?
questions.hint: Flamenco developed primarily in Andalusia, southern Spain, blending music, singing, and dance.

questions.question: Which species of bear is the largest living land carnivore?
questions.hint: Polar bears are generally considered the largest living land carnivores, with some males exceeding 700 kg (1,540 lb).

questions.question: Which river is the second-longest in South America after the Amazon?
questions.hint: The Paraná River flows through Brazil, Paraguay, and Argentina for nearly 4,900 kilometers.

questions.question: Which gas is the second most abundant in Earth's atmosphere?
questions.hint: Earth's atmosphere is approximately 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, with argon and other gases making up the remainder.

questions.question: Which civilization developed the first known urban sanitation and drainage systems?
questions.hint: Cities such as Mohenjo-daro and Harappa featured remarkably advanced drainage, sewage, and urban planning over 4,000 years ago.
